summary: Our project is significant because it can assist future astronauts and inhabitants of Mars through our survival guide. We have developed several prototypes, such as the "Astra" bracelet, which monitors vital signs and oxygen levels; it also enables communication with our assistant, "Deimos." By addressing the challenges of survival in the Martian environment, our project aims to facilitate future missions and settlements, taking into account health, risks, and the various situations that astronauts might encounter.
details:
We are Team Deimos, and our project is an interplanetary survival guide: Mars Map.

What does it do or how does it work? Our project is an AI-driven initiative designed to assist in our expedition to Mars. It is divided into several prototypes: We have a wristband worn on the forearm, whose function is to send messages from Mars to planet Earth in the shortest possible time. This is made possible by an AI that evaluates the severity of the message—for example, a lack of oxygen for the astronaut. The message will be sent as quickly as possible to those monitoring from the other side. Additionally, we have developed Deimos, an AI-integrated robot that provides support in various ways, such as emotional support and the creation of routes classified by their level of risk. It accompanies the astronaut and incorporates expert advice that will simplify the Martian expedition. ASTRA is the core application of this project. It contains several essential sections for a successful expedition, featuring a 3D map with the most prominent landmarks on Mars, such as Olympus Mons (the largest volcano in the solar system and the highest mountain on Mars). Furthermore, the routes previously mapped out by Deimos are logged into the expedition map. It also integrates other sections such as health, map view, nutrition, etc.

What benefits does it offer? This project provides numerous benefits for exploration and survival on Mars, as it allows astronauts to carry out their expeditions with greater safety and confidence, reducing the risks associated with the extreme conditions of their habitat. It offers practical accompaniment, recommendations, and guidance through the 3D map, in addition to the analysis and information provided by Deimos and the ASTRA application. Likewise, it facilitates emergency communication with Earth by prioritizing messages according to their severity, and it provides both physical and emotional support to the astronaut. In this way, it contributes to a more organized, safe, and efficient exploration, optimizing decision-making and allowing astronauts to focus on their research and discoveries

What is the expected impact of the project? We anticipate that, for future generations, exploring this planet will be much easier, as there will be proper preparation and thorough knowledge of the various sectors of the Martian environment. Additionally, we will better understand the different phenomena that occur there, such as marsquakes, storms, radiation, etc. We must recognize that mental health is just as important as physical health; therefore, as expeditions become more routine, in the distant future more and more people will be able to travel there, and the likelihood of developing emotional symptoms will decrease (since those who go on space expeditions generally report developing emotional challenges). With this, in the near future, alongside the development of more futuristic technologies that complement this project, it could become possible to inhabit this planet.

In what sense is your project creative? We believe it is creative because we have envisioned diverse scenarios illustrating what it would be like to safely visit planet Mars. Moreover, at certain stages of developing the project's features, we put ourselves in the shoes of the lead Martian explorer. Through this approach, we identified what kind of innovation we would need so that exploration and the survival guide go hand in hand.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project? We used AI—specifically AI Studio—working with the Python programming language in an environment similar to Visual Studio. Gemini was also used to generate several images and conduct research that helped improve the project. Similarly, relevant NASA data and resources were utilized, such as the Mars Global Surveyor (MGS), Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity Rover), and the NASA Phoenix Mars Lander. In addition, physical models and equations calibrated with NASA data were implemented, including the Martian Barometric Law based on MOLA Elevation, Ionizing Dosimetry models by Atmospheric Column, and the Composite Survival and Habitability Index (0–100).
